name: dashpot-latch
title: Dashpot Latch
description: A destructive-action drawer sealed by a viscous damper: a flick moves the handle an inch and oozes it back, only a slow, sustained pull glides it home at a capped speed.
useWhen: a destructive confirm gated on the VELOCITY of a moving drag, not the duration of a static press — the same distance covered fast fails and covered slowly succeeds, so the gesture is physically hard to perform by accident or in anger. Pick hold-to-confirm instead when the control has no travel of its own and confirmation should just cost a fixed press-and-hold duration.
instruction: A destructive-action confirm rendered as a rail with a draggable handle, gated on gesture VELOCITY rather than press duration or absolute pointer position. The handle's progress (0-1, the only thing that decides its position) is integrated on a rAF loop from a simulated viscous damper: handleVelocity = min(pointerVelocity, vMax) (default 80px/s), where pointerVelocity is an EMA of the pointer's instantaneous dx/dt — so a flick (high instantaneous speed, released almost immediately) only ever buys a sliver of travel before it oozes back to zero, and a mid-drag yank (instantaneous speed past 3x vMax) actively bleeds progress backward at oozeRate (default 40px/s) even while still held down, with a small random jitter shudder on the handle while overspeed. Only a slow, sustained pull — velocity kept under the overspeed threshold, held until the fill saturates and sits at 100% for a final 200ms — commits; releasing at any point before that lets the same 40px/s ooze carry the handle back home. Progress fill renders in the muted token and flips to the accent token only in the final 10% of travel, marking the commit point as a legitimate accent use (interaction feedback, not decoration). All handle transform / fill width / ring dashoffset writes happen directly to the DOM once per rAF tick; React state changes only at the confirmed transition. The keyboard path mirrors the same gate rather than sidestepping it: holding Enter or Space arms a visible countdown ring for kbHoldMs (default 1500ms) and releasing early recoils exactly like an under-speed pointer release, so repeated tapping just keeps resetting the ring; aria-describedby on the handle carries a hint explaining to pull slowly, and a polite aria-live region announces 25/50/75% progress crossings, since the drag/hold physics sit on top of one real button and screen reader users get plain progress text against an ordinary control, not a shape they can't perceive. prefers-reduced-motion keeps the velocity gate exactly as-is (it is the safety mechanism, not decoration) and only drops the overspeed jitter shudder. Distinct from hold-to-confirm: that control gates on the duration of a static press with no travel of its own; this one gates on the velocity profile of a moving gesture, so the same distance covered fast fails and covered slowly succeeds. Zero dependencies, DOM+SVG+CSS only (no canvas), colors only from --background --foreground --muted --border --accent, tears down its ResizeObserver/IntersectionObserver/media-query listener and rAF on unmount.
